assertions: Sir William Waller will overcome in the engagement of this day, 29 March 1644, near Alresford / Cheriton; the victory falls to Waller's Parliamentarian side, not to Hopton

Sir Ralph Hopton will be defeated and forced to give ground / retreat: his significator Saturn is in his fall, peregrine, sub radiis, and in no aspect to any planet, so his side has no strength, no direction and no effective support in the fight

Waller's assistants and substance are strong and honourably placed: the Sun, lord of Waller's 2nd (his assistants / supplies), is in the 10th house in the very degree of his exaltation, 19 degrees Aries, so his officers and aid act powerfully and openly for him

Hopton will lack ready supplies and reserves: in the house bearing on his supplies there are only Mars and the South Node, showing no supplies ready for him and diminution / loss rather than reinforcement

Momentum grows for Waller during the action itself: the Moon, co-significator of Waller's side, is in her exaltation with Jupiter, swift in motion and increasing in light, and distant 11 degrees from Venus, so Waller's fortune strengthens rather than fades as the battle proceeds

The decision comes on the day of the figure itself, not by delay or a drawn stalemate: the figure was erected the day of the engagement and Waller's significators are angular, exalted and swift, while Hopton's significator aspects the cusp of his own 7th by square, afflicting his own side
method: Lilly horary astrology (Christian Astrology Book II): 1st house / Ascendant side for Waller vs 7th house lord Saturn for Hopton, judged by essential and accidental dignity, solar condition, aspects and house placement
reasoning: Waller's side (Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, Venus) is dignified on every count given in the figure: Moon in exaltation with Jupiter, swift and increasing in light; Sun lord of Waller's 2nd in the 10th in his exact exaltation degree 19 Aries, giving strong assistants in honour. Hopton's side is the mirror opposite: Saturn lord of the 7th is in fall, peregrine, sub radiis, unaspected by any planet, and squaring his own 7th cusp, and his supplies are shown only by Mars with the South Node, i.e. none ready. Strong, angular, exalted querent-side significators against a fallen, combust-adjacent, isolated opponent significator gives a decisive, same-day victory for Waller. This is a single-point battle question with no near/far two-stage process, so no second-stage outcome is asserted.
summary: Waller should overcome Hopton in the battle of 29 March 1644; Hopton is defeated and retreats for want of strength and supplies.
